speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol abuse or exposure to heavy metals? Also, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or loss of vibration sense in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any new neurological symptoms such as vision changes, weakness, or cognitive difficulties since starting natalizumab? REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are classic for Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), a known complication of natalizumab therapy. I will confirm the diagnosis with a CSF analysis for JC virus DNA. REQUEST TEST: CSF_JCV_DNA_PCR

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative CSF PCR is concerning, but given the classic MRI findings and clinical presentation in a natalizumab-treated patient, PML remains the leading diagnosis as PCR sensitivity can be variable in early stages. I will review the brain MRI images directly to assess the lesion characteristics and rule out other differentials. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative CSF PCR is a critical finding that casts doubt on the PML diagnosis, especially given the lack of fever or other systemic symptoms. I need to rule out other causes of demyelination or ataxia, such as autoimmune conditions or vitamin deficiencies related to your Crohn's disease. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Vitamin_B12_and_Folate

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal B12 levels, I must reconsider the diagnosis despite the classic MRI appearance. Has your Crohn's disease involved the terminal ileum, and have you undergone any recent surgeries that might affect bile acid absorption?

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the normal B12 and negative JCV PCR, the MRI findings and clinical context strongly suggest PML, as early CSF PCR can be falsely negative. I will proceed with a definitive diagnosis based on the characteristic radiological evidence and natalizumab exposure. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
